_comment: Reading order, level, and per-story stretch vocabulary. Replaces the hardcoded ORDER list in index.py, which does not survive a growing corpus. Levels are defined once and stories declare one, so a new story slots into an existing rung rather than inventing another. Construction names here must match the keys in stats.py's GRAMMAR_PATTERNS.

budgets._comment: Rates, not counts, so they scale with story length: a fixed '5+ occurrences per new word' would have spent 5.7% of the shortest story's content tokens on two words, which reads as engineered. The mandatory requirement is qualitative and no script checks it — a new word's FIRST occurrence must sit in a sentence that frames its meaning. WHERE EACH NUMBER CAME FROM is ../CALIBRATION.md: the reference band against 25 authentic 児童文学 texts, why subordinate_share is measured and not gated, why min_sentence_stdev must not be raised, and five recorded corrections. That prose lived here until 2026-09-16 and was 97% of this block by weight, five values' worth, one unwrapped line per key.

defaults._comment: What a story is briefed to be when nothing is said. Resolution order is explicit argument, then this block; every parameter has a default so a bare invocation works. Defaults live here rather than in AUTHORING.md prose because a default nothing reads is a suggestion. `pages` is the unit because it is what the reader shows; tokens are derived, and every rate budget scales from tokens. null means derive from `budgets` at story length.

registers._comment: Five object-centred, quiet, past-tense stories closing on a concrete image is a house style that fell out of the recycling requirement rather than a decision anyone made. Naming it makes it a choice. Two of the alternatives already exist in the corpus as undeclared one-offs. Register changes voice and structure; it never relaxes the narrow-domain rule, because the object at the centre is the recycling engine.
registers.quiet-realism: the default and the current five: one concrete object at the centre, close narration, ends on an image rather than a claim
registers.folktale: 城の鐘: nested time frames, a told-to-you voice, the turn stated once in dialogue
registers.procedural: 猫を探す探偵: a clue planted early and paid off late, the reader able to reach the answer from facts already on the page
registers.ghost-story: none yet, the 怪談 shape: the ordinary held steady until one detail is wrong, and the wrong detail is never explained. Ends on the ordinary resuming, not on a reveal — nobody names what happened and no character theorises about it, which is also what keeps it off the closing-thesis defect. Two guards, both from the September 2026 reviews. The dead must not be a relative the protagonist is mourning: 時計の音 and 煙突の煙 are that story twice and were rated ★2 both times, the second explicitly as derivative of the first, so grief is not what this register is for. And the wrong detail has to be retrievable — planted concretely, payable from facts already on the page — because 縁台の将棋 was marked down for a twist that was obvious and a premise that was never stated, which are the two ways this shape fails.
registers.retrospective: 廊下の鏡, the 述懐 voice: an older narrator looking back, long subordinated sentences as the shape of memory, ends on a claim rather than an image. The claim is about the WORLD — a person, the object, a fact the narrator now holds — never about what the story means; that second thing is the closing-thesis defect cut from four of five stories in September 2026, and this register sits closer to it than any other. The guard that makes it safe is that the narrator earns the claim by watching a physical event, so the last page reports a correction of fact rather than a conclusion.

levels._comment: A level is a rung, not a checklist. `min_present` is how many of the level's own constructions a story must actually use; the rest are available, not required. `min_carried` is the fraction of every LOWER level's constructions the story should still exercise, which is what makes it a ladder rather than five disjoint sets. Level 5 deliberately has a low min_present: a few marked N2 forms inside otherwise-N3 prose is the 'flirting with N2' band, and requiring all of them would be the wall this is meant to avoid.

stories.title: 時計の音
stories._new_words: Declared here rather than in approved-words.json, which stays a short global list of permanent allowances. These are per-story teaching words: all four are the story's own subject matter, so they recur without the prose working at it. check.py does not flag them because the particle-splitting fallback accepts 部品 as 部+品 and 歯車 as 歯+車, so they have to be declared to be marked.

new_words.部品: watch parts — framed by the drawer of sorted boxes before it is ever used alone
new_words.歯車: gear — framed as the contents of the smallest box, too small to hold in the fingers
new_words.針: hand of a watch — framed p7 by the already-known 秒針 in the line before it, 細い秒針まではっきり見えた, so the bare 針 arrives as the set that second hand belongs to. Carries the stopped-at-three-ten thread, and the night the watch runs for hours without a hand advancing
new_words.振り子: pendulum — framed by the wall of shop clocks all swinging at the same speed

new_words.便箋: letter paper — framed p8 by 中から、折った便箋が一枚だけ出てきた with the blank lower half described in the next line; recurs as the son's sheet, hers, and the reply's
new_words.消印: postmark — framed p4 by position first and contents second, 切手の上の消印を読んで、日にちを数えた followed by 小さな丸の中に、遠い町の名前と三月四日が押してある; later dates the son's wait and identifies the reply's origin
new_words.表札: nameplate — framed p1 by 玄関の横の表札を確かめると、そこは松田という私の名字になっている, which is the right-address/wrong-name premise made physical. Passes check.py via the 表+札 fallback, so it must be declared to be marked

stories.title: 終電
stories._feature: Untagged two-person dialogue. 38 of 39 quoted lines carry no attribution and the train conversation is 100% untagged, with speakers held by register: he asks, at length and over-politely, and she answers short. The single kept attribution is the manager's remembered line on page 4, so the reader sees one tagged line before the mode changes. Longest untagged run is 10, against 1 and 2 in the stories either side. Measured 2026-09-19: her replies run 2 to 22 characters against a median of 9, so the cue is question-versus-answer and register, not a length band — an earlier version of this key claimed four to eight and was never true of either draft.

new_words.網棚: luggage rack — framed p3 by the narrator's own aborted use of it, 荷物を網棚に上げようとして、やめた, with 足元に置いておく方が、降りる時に楽だ fixing it against the floor in the next line. It is the object of the first exchange with her and the closing image of that thread
new_words.乗客: passenger — framed p3 by a count in a car already called 空いている, 今夜も車内には乗客が四人しかいなくて、皆、離れた席に座っていた; tracks the train emptying until only the two of them are left

stories.title: 煙突の煙
stories._note: The first story written through the two-gate flow: brief resolved and confirmed before drafting, premise and afterword written in English before any Japanese existed.
stories._premise: A woman returns for a week to clear her late father's apartment and goes to the neighbourhood bathhouse every evening of its last week. The owner has been keeping the water hot past closing for three months, waiting for a regular who came late from the factory. That regular was her father, and nobody told the owner he had died. Beats, each joined by だから or しかし: (1) clearing the apartment, chimney visible from the window / (2) as a child, the smoke going out meant he was on his way home / (3) first evening, closing Sunday, almost no customers / (4) the owner does not recognise her and says nothing / (5) PLANT: one 桶 kept aside, upside down, never handed out / (6) she says nothing and keeps returning to look for it / (7) the smoke keeps going up after closing, every night / (8) she asks; he says he is waiting for a regular from the factory / (9) TURN: she works out who, and that she never told him / (10) she tells him; he turns the 桶 over and fills it; from the window the smoke stops early for the first time.

new_words.湯気: steam — framed p5 by 戸を開けると、湯気が外へ流れ出した, so the word is shown doing something visible before anything is said about it, and the fogged mirrors follow in the next line. Recurs over the bath, off the filled 桶 at the turn, and under the ceiling on the last night
new_words.桶: washing bucket — framed p7 as the thing you fetch for yourself, 桶は棚から自分で取る, with the stack described bottoms-up in the next line. The one left mouth-up is the story's plant and its payoff, so it repeats without the prose reaching
new_words.番台: the raised attendant's desk — framed p6 by what crosses it rather than by what it is: the owner takes the money without a word and passes the soap up from underneath. It is where he is in every scene until he climbs down from it at the turn
new_words.煙突: chimney — framed p2 by 煙突は町のどの建物よりも高いので、この部屋からでもよく見える, which is the reason the signalling works at all. Carries that thread: the childhood memory, the smoke after closing, and the last line
new_words.湯船: the bath itself, as against washing — framed p8 by 体を洗ってから、湯船に入った and immediately by being too hot to get into. Recurs at the close, where she does not stop
new_words.廃業: going out of business — framed p4 by the notice at the door, 今度の日曜日で廃業する、と書いてあった, and by the narrator standing and reading the word. Deliberately paired against the already-known 閉店, which stays in the story for the nightly closing hour: 閉店の時間は過ぎているはずだった is what makes her look up at the smoke, and 廃業 is what the week is counting down to. Added 2026-09-19; brief.new_words raised 5 to 6 for it

stories.title: 縁台の将棋
stories._note: The first story briefed with a deliberately widened new-word budget, at 2.4x the derived rate, and the first with no death in it. Both came out of the 2026-09-19 second blind read: six evaluators named circumlocution-around-the-obligatory-noun as the corpus's clearest tell, and the reader's own ★2 on 煙突の煙 said 'another story about a dead person, derivative of the watch story'. The extra budget is spent entirely on the board, because the people could already be written — 座る, 隣, 向かい, 膝, 髪, 耳, 息, 手袋 are all known, so nothing in the relationship needed a new word.
stories._premise: Two women meet every Sunday over a shogi board on a park bench. The younger, the narrator, wins almost every week, because Hiroko resigns around the fortieth move. Hiroko is in fact much the stronger player and has been resigning from winning positions for a year: a game she wins is a game that ends, and the narrator would go home. the narrator, meanwhile, has been studying alone every night for the same reason, to make the games last. Her studying is what exposes it. Beats, each joined by だから or しかし: (1) the Sunday ritual, the bench, the pieces going down / (2) PLANT: Hiroko resigns on move forty and the narrator does not understand how she won / (3) the narrator buys a book so the next game will last longer / (4) weeks pass, the games run to seventy moves, the resignation still arrives / (5) the narrator starts watching Hiroko's fingertips instead of the board, and the pause does not look like losing / (6) a cold Sunday, gloves off, red cheeks, the closest they come to saying anything / (7) the narrator gives check for the first time and Hiroko resigns early / (8) TURN: the narrator rebuilds the abandoned position from Hiroko's side and finds mate in two / (9) a year of Sundays reorganises itself; both of them had been playing to keep the other there / (10) the next Sunday Hiroko moves first, plays it out, wins, and asks for a second game for the first time.
stories._new_words: Twelve, against a derived five. Held at twelve rather than higher because every declared word must reach min_occurrences, and 駒台 and 盤面 would have had to be reached for — the documented failure. Each of these is either the subject matter or load-bearing for the turn.

new_words.将棋: shogi — the subject; framed p1 by being played rather than described, 日曜日の午後、私はそこで将棋を指す
new_words.駒: piece — framed p2 by being set out and making a sound, never explained. The story's highest-frequency new word
new_words.盤: board — framed p2 by Hiroko sitting across it. Carries the last beat, where half of it falls into shadow
new_words.指す: to play a move — the verb the domain takes rather than する or やる, framed p1 in the opening sentence of the ritual
new_words.対局: a game, as a unit — framed p2 as the thing that begins once the pieces are out. Needed because the story counts games across a year
new_words.縁台: the wooden bench — framed p1 by being the place, and it is where every scene happens. Title word
new_words.持ち駒: pieces in hand — framed p11 by being counted during the reconstruction, which is the mechanism of the turn, and again p18 as they dwindle
new_words.王手: check — framed p10 by the narrator giving it for the first time, which is what triggers the early resignation. Returns at p20 against her
new_words.詰み: mate — framed p5 as the thing the book is teaching her, どうやって作られるのか, and it is what she finds on the abandoned board
new_words.投了: resignation — framed p3 by Hiroko doing it, and it is the story's plant. Recurs as the weekly ritual and stops recurring at the end, which is the payoff
new_words.指先: fingertips — framed p7 by the narrator watching them instead of the board. The crush made physical, and the tell that the pause is a choice
new_words.頬: cheek — framed p8 by being red in December. Returns at the end still red, when it is not the cold

stories.title: 三番の乾燥機
stories._note: The first story with every brief parameter moved off its default, at the reader's request. Two of them are attributable and the brief is the only record either way. `dialogue` 28% untagged comes from the reader's ★4 on 終電 — 'brief and aloof interaction, a quiet connection' — which is the corpus's only rating above ★3 and runs 29.8% dialogue at 97.4% untagged; it landed at 26.5% and 100%. `new_words` 12 comes from the 2026-09-19 second blind read, where six evaluators converged on circumlocution-around-the-obligatory-noun as the clearest tell and 23 of 24 obligatory nouns tested outside the known set. The domain was chosen by measurement rather than taste: have.py over ~160 words across three candidate domains put the room, the machines and the people of a coin laundry almost entirely inside the known set, so the whole widened budget goes on obligatory nouns and nothing is spent on the relationship. A bakery was rejected on the same test (窯, 生地, 粉, 小麦 all outside), which is the institutional-setting failure that second read named. Second story running with nobody dead in it and nothing anybody's keepsake.
stories._premise: A man who has just moved onto the shopping street does his laundry at the all-night coin laundry every Tuesday, and every Tuesday an older woman is in the same chair under the heater, reading, with a very small bag of washing and the one dryer that does not get warm. She washes very little and runs the cold machine through twice, which takes two hours. Annoyed after carrying his own wash home half dry, he tells the owner the machine is broken; a notice goes up; the following week she is finished and gone in thirty minutes. Beats, each joined by だから or しかし: (1) Tuesdays at the coin laundry, because the new flat has no machine / (2) PLANT: he learns the room by watching it, and the woman under the heater has a magazine, one small bag, and never leaves / (3) a cold night, only number three free, and his wash comes out cold — 乾いているはずだった / (4) 「三番は温まらない」, said to her magazine after the fact, and he does not answer / (5) weeks of not speaking, and the anomaly: she takes number three every week, on purpose, and runs it twice / (6) short exchanges accumulate over the winter — 「二番がいちばん速い」, 「あなたには、ね」 — and he cannot stop doing the arithmetic / (7) half helpfulness and half still being annoyed, he tells the owner to put a notice on it / (8) PAYOFF: she reads the notice, takes number four, and is out the door in thirty minutes; the chair under the heater is empty before nine / (9) the owner, counting him a regular now, asks him to mind the place for the repairman / (10) TURN: 「別に、悪くないです」 — the notice comes down, she puts her bag back in number three, and he puts his own wash in beside it knowing it will not dry.
stories._new_words: Nine, against a derived six and a briefed ceiling of twelve. Held there rather than filled to twelve because the ceiling is not a target and every one had to clear min_occurrences without the prose reaching for it: the shortest runs four times, the longest thirteen. Every one is an obligatory noun of the domain, and two of them — 貼り紙 and 無人 — are named in the 2026-09-19 second blind read as words this corpus had previously written around, as 「紙」 and as 「空」.

new_words.コインランドリー: coin laundry — the setting. Framed p1 by being walked to with an armful of washing, never described. Page 4 is the de-circumlocution: このコインランドリーに通うようになって rather than ここへ. Declared for the record only: Ichiran segments it into コイン + ランドリー and build.py analyses kanji words alone, so both halves ship with no n, no u and no kana — the katakana case AUTHORING.md already names for クロ, where the marker earns nothing because there is no reading to teach
new_words.乾燥機: dryer — the story's object and its highest-frequency new word at ten. Framed p2 by wet things being moved across into one, which is what a dryer is for
new_words.洗濯物: the washing, as a noun — thirteen occurrences. Framed p1 in the arms of somebody carrying it. Load-bearing for the arithmetic, because the size of hers against the size of his is the clue
new_words.温まる: to get warm, intransitive — the story's key predicate, and the sentence the whole plot turns on is 「三番は温まらない」. Framed p12 as a consequence, spoken to a magazine after his wash has already failed. 四番は温まる at p26 is the same word doing the payoff
new_words.貼り紙: a notice stuck up — framed p24 by being stuck on the machine, and it is the hinge: it goes up because he asked for it and comes down because he lies. Written as 「紙」 in 猫を探す探偵, which the second blind read caught
new_words.小銭: coins — framed p2 by being fed into a machine. Runs from not having enough on his first night to having them ready in his bag on the last page, which is the only place the story says he has changed twice
new_words.商店街: the shopping street — framed p1 as the place walked down, and it is what he goes back out into at p12 with the half-dry shirts
new_words.無人: unstaffed — framed p3 as the consequence of the owner shutting up at nine, an event rather than a definition. Carries the last movement: it is why a 留守番 is needed at all, and 無人のはずの店 at p30 is the night he is the one in it. Written as 「空」 in 終電, which the second blind read caught
new_words.生乾き: half dry — framed p11 by coming out of the machine that way after eighty minutes. The word he uses to the owner at p24, which is what makes the complaint land

stories._voice: Failure mode six, measured with voice.py after the draft. past_pct 59.8 against an authentic median of 59.3 and final3_entropy 5.74 against a median 5.45 are both the best in the corpus, and final3_top3_pct 20.5 sits on the authentic median of 20.2. run_mean is 3.90 against an authentic 2.24-3.37 and is left there on purpose. The first draft ran run_max 15 and run_mean 4.46; three changes took it to 13 and 3.90, and every one was a prose fix rather than a variety purchase — a scenic ル sentence inside the December scene, a grudge that is still live so its sentence is not past either (今でも思う), and a past event moved out of ことも覚えている into plain past. What is left driving run_mean is two long ル blocks, 11 and 13 sentences, and those are the habitual establishing passages: Japanese habitual narration is ル, and breaking them would be the documented failure of buying a number. AUTHORING.md's own test is the stretch where every sentence lands on the same ENDING, and the entropy figure says this story does not have one.
stories._mimetics: Ten, planned into the draft rather than added to it: ぐるぐる on the drum at p7, p30 and the last line, がたがた on the old machine at p8, きょろきょろ on his first night at p4, ぽかぽか and いい匂い on a load out of a dryer that works at p26, はっと at p28, そっと at p26, ばったり at p22. Measured 2026-09-19 the corpus ran 0.34 per 100 narration sentences against an authentic 4.35-33.12; the figure says where to look, not what to hit, and where to look was narration that reports motion where it could depict it. No 三点リーダー: measured Dead, the authentic median is 0.00 and this corpus's zero already is that median.

stories.title: 猫を探す探偵
stories._feature: A plot held across 30 pages: the boxes clue is planted on page 8 and not recalled until page 21, and the reader is expected to reach the answer from facts already on the page. The second plant is the detective's own: a book borrowed at twelve and never returned, p22, which makes his decision about the boy a fact about him rather than a position he argues. The story now ends on that book, the cold office and a fee that does not cover the rent. THE NO-THESIS EXCEPTION WAS RETIRED 2026-09-19. This key used to read 'the one exception to the no-thesis rule; it is allowed to state its closing claim outright', which licensed the last two lines, 探偵の仕事は真実を見つけることじゃない。見つけた真実をどうするかだ。 Four evaluators independently named that pair as the clearest proof of an English short-story pattern in the corpus. The afterword mechanism now says it in English on the last page, which is where it belongs, so the lines are cut and the exception does not survive them.
stories._new_words: This story's four teaching words predate the per-story mechanism and still live in approved-words.json, where they are marked correctly. Left there rather than moved, to avoid churn; new stories should declare theirs here instead.

stories.title: 城の鐘
stories._feature: Nested time frames: a story told in the past about a casting forty years earlier. The distinction everything turns on is stated exactly once, in dialogue, on page 12. Level 5 is the sparse N2 edge, four such forms used once each.
stories._note: 王, 従う, 罰, 叫ぶ and 段/二百段 predate the per-story mechanism and remain in approved-words.json. 段 is the weakest of them as a teaching word: two of its six occurrences sit inside 二百段, which Ichiran parses as a single token, so the reader marks the unit rather than teaching the counter.

new_words.響く: to resound, carry — a bell story needs the verb. Framed p8 by explicit contrast: 形の良い鐘は打った後も音が長く響き、悪い鐘は音がすぐに途切れる. Recurs at the king's death, the princess's bad bell, the palm on the tower bell, and the apprentice's strike
new_words.金属: metal — framed p3 by melting and heat, 金属を溶かす日だけ、部屋は息ができないほど熱くなる, then poured, cooled, and made thin at the top. Accepted by check.py via the 金+属 fallback, so it must be declared to be marked

stories.title: 行かなかった人の地図
stories._feature: The longest story in the corpus and the first with a supernatural element. folktale register carries the magic for free: the 主 on the pass is furniture, nobody explains it, and it costs nothing from the new-word budget because 主, 姿, 影, 声, 問う, 通す are all known. The 主 scene also gives the にとって focus a structural home, asking all three travellers the same question.
stories._note: grammar_focus にとって was chosen because the construction and the theme are the same thing: one object meaning something different to each person who holds it. It lands four times, once per holder — 祖父 p5, 甚平 p19, 蓮 p24, 梓 p27 — which is the set the 主 scene is built to collect. 地図のとおりに is the other repeated frame and carries とおり. MEETS ITS PAGE BRIEF AT 44 (briefed 40, band 36-44). This note used to record a 48-page MISS and blame the brief: 'a twelve-beat structure with a six-page set piece in the middle does not fit in 40 pages'. That was wrong, and the 2026-09-19 revision is the proof — all twelve beats and the whole 主 scene are still here at 44. What did not fit was the over-explanation: the two definitional lines that handed the reader 峠 and 崖 outright (峠というのは、山と山の間の、一番低いところである / 崖とは、岩が真っ直ぐに立っているところである), and the narrator restating what a scene had just shown (人が歩けば足跡が残るのだから…). Both words are now framed by what happens to them instead. The brief was reachable; the prose was not yet tight.
stories._premise: 梓's grandfather spent fifty years drawing one map, of a mountain road he never walked, copied from his father's telling. Dying, he asks her to go and see whether the tree at the end of it is still standing. She hires 甚平, an old guide who crosses those mountains without maps, and every landmark on the paper turns out to be wrong. Beats, each joined by だから or しかし: (1) the dying grandfather asks her to check the tree / (2) 甚平 reads the map once and says the bridge is in the wrong place / (3) three days in, every landmark matches and 蓮 stops laughing / (4) PLANT: no bridge at the river, and four small 印 beside it on the map that she cannot explain / (5) the detour along the 岸 and up to the 峠 / (6) the 主 asks each of them what they came to do; 梓's answer is her grandfather's, not her own / (7) at the 崖 the road is missing, 蓮 says an old man drew a road out of stories, and 甚平 finds the road under the slide / (8) the village on the map is empty, no 足跡 / (9) TURN, once, in dialogue: 千代 remembers the bridge falling the year of the great snow, seventy-five years ago, five years before the grandfather was born / (10) PAYOFF: the 印 are counts of how many times his father told of each landmark, so the map is scaled to memory rather than distance / (11) the tree is there, and the sea, which on the map is one straight blue line / (12) home: he does not ask about the tree, he asks whether the sea was blue.

new_words.印: mark — the story's own subject matter and its plant. Framed p4 by the act of making one, 祖父が地図へ小さな印を一つ書き足すのを見たことがある, a page after the already-known 目印 it will turn out to be counting. Recurs at the bridge, the village, the rock and the tree, and is what the turn is made of
new_words.頼る: to rely on — framed p1 by the villagers who will not use the map, then sharpened p9 in 蓮's challenge, 行ったことのない人が描いた地図に頼るんですか, where the object of the reliance is the whole question of the story. Recurs whenever the map is trusted or set aside
new_words.導く: to lead, guide — framed p6 by the one name the whole village gives her, あの男が導いてくれる, and again p23 by 甚平's answer to the 主, この二人を北へ導くために来た, beside the already-known 案内 in the same breath. The guide's own word for what he does
new_words.峠: mountain pass — framed p17 without a definition: 甚平 draws two mountains in the dirt, presses his finger into the low place between them and names it, 岸を上って、ここを越える。峠だ. The setting of the 主 scene and the middle third of the journey
new_words.崖: cliff — framed p29 by what it does to the sky, 道の右側に岩が立ち上がって、上の方は空しか見えなくなった, one line before the map shows a road running beneath one. Carries the buried-road beat that proves the map is early rather than false
new_words.岩: rock, boulder — named p3 in the map's list of landmarks, then framed p11 as the first of them to match, with her hand on it: 真ん中から二つに割れていて、割れ目に草が生えている. Recurs as the split rock, the rock slope of the climb, and the slide at the 崖
new_words.岸: riverbank — framed p13 by the width of the water, 流れは速く、向こうの岸は遠い, then p14 by walking it and finding nothing standing on it. The detour is three days of that
new_words.足跡: footprint — framed p18 by 甚平 reading tracks in the earth and naming what is not in them, 動物の足跡ばかりで、人の足跡は一つもない. Marks the empty village p33, and the party's own are the last thing in the grass before the climb

stories.title: 廊下の鏡
stories._feature: First story in the retrospective (述懐) register, and the first in the corpus to end on a claim rather than an image. The register was added for it. Also the first multi-construction grammar_focus: ものの, 一方で and にとって together, chosen because concession, contrast and perspective are the three things a looking-back voice actually does, so the focus and the register reinforce each other instead of the focus being sprinkled on afterwards.
stories._note: THE RISK IS THE ENDING and it was named at Gate 2 before drafting. 'Ends on a claim' sits one step from the closing-thesis defect. The guard is that the claim corrects a fact about a PERSON — 祖母は、不思議なことを信じる人ではなかった — and contradicts a phrase the reader has already been given in dialogue on p10, 「おばあさんは、不思議なことを信じる人だから」. It is a correction, not a moral, and the narrator earns it by watching the hallway go dark rather than by concluding anything. THE MIRROR IS NEVER A FIGURE: it is cleaned, wrapped, carried, cracked, lifted and re-hung, and the prose never once uses it for memory or for looking back. That was a standing constraint from Rob, not a discovery. Every clue is physical and early: it hangs where nobody dresses, it faces a window rather than a room, it is polished on bright days and not dull ones, she is twice shown cleaning it and never once looking into it, and the child needs no lamp at the turn.
stories._premise: A mirror hangs at the turn of a dark hallway in one house for sixty years, through a grandmother, a mother and a daughter, each of whom polishes it, wraps it and hangs it back on the same nail. Only when the last of them takes the house apart and lifts it off the wall does she find out what it was for: hung at an angle to the one window, it carried light around the corner into the windowless back of the house. Beats, each joined by だから or しかし: (1) the narrator, 71, is emptying the house and leaves the heavy mirror for last / (2) she notices she has worked all day at the turn without a lamp and thinks nothing of it, because she never has / (3) the grandmother carried the mirror in when she married, chose its place herself, and asked one thing, 動かさないでください / (4) she polished it constantly and only on clear days; PLANT: 一方で, never once seen looking at her own reflection / (5) the family settled on 不思議なことを信じる人, stated in dialogue / (6) she died and nobody moved it, the instruction outliving the reason / (7) the mother kept the rule without the reason, and at the roof repair wrapped it herself and made the workmen return the nail to the same hole / (8) asked why, she could only say her mother had asked her not to / (9) the narrator read all of it as a keepsake and stopped thinking / (10) TURN, physical and not a realization: she lifts it off the nail to wrap it and the back of the hallway goes dark around her while she is holding it / (11) she puts it back three times, and by the third is counting years rather than checking / (12) PAYOFF: the polishing, the weather and the averted eyes all resolve at once / (13) the claim, once: 祖母は、不思議なことを信じる人ではなかった.

new_words.光: light, as a noun — the thing the mirror actually carries, and deliberately withheld until the payoff. 光る is already known, so the noun is the new form. Framed at the turn by 光が、曲がり角を回って奥に届いた, where the sentence before it has just shown the hallway going dark. Recurs through the resolution
new_words.斜め: at an angle — the mechanism of the whole story. Framed p7 by contrast with the flat alternative, 壁と同じ向きにまっすぐ掛けるのではなく、少し斜めにした. Recurs at the roof repair, where the mother restores the angle, and at the payoff
new_words.釘: nail — what fixes the position across three generations. Framed p2 by the act itself, 壁に釘を一本打って、そこに掛けた. Recurs as the same hole at the repair, as 三代、同じ釘, and at the lifting off
new_words.向き: the way a thing faces, orientation — distinct from 斜め, which is that the orientation is oblique. Framed p7 in the same sentence that introduces 斜め, 壁と同じ向きに, and fixed by the already-known 向く in the next line, 鏡は玄関の窓のほうを向いている. Recurs wherever the mirror is set or restored
new_words.埃: dust — why the polishing was frequent rather than fussy, and it is held back as an explanation until the payoff. Framed p9 by its own absence, 埃がついていなくても、晴れた日には必ず磨く, which makes the polishing strange before it makes it sensible

stories.title: 十五日の質札
stories._feature: First story in the ghost-story register, and the first written against the September 2026 Gate 2 — climax first, want and need on separate tracks, a declared three-act shape, every beat a yes-but or a no-and. The veiled plant is bookkeeping: the narrator spoils a ticket in the first week and voids it by number, which reads as him being tired and pays off as the only proof the story offers.
stories._note: THE GHOST IS NOT A MOURNED RELATIVE. That guard is written into the register itself because 時計の音 and 煙突の煙 are the same bereavement story twice and were rated two stars both times, the second explicitly as derivative. The woman is a stranger and the weight sits on the narrator's choice, not on her condition. THE TWIST IS NOT THAT SHE IS DEAD — a reader will suspect that by the neighbour scene, and it is meant to be suspected. The turn is the ticket number, and under it the fact that he confessed to someone who was never going to catch him. THE FATHER IS A SOURCE OF A RULE AND NOTHING ELSE: he is named three times, never mourned, and the story does not visit him. YEAR-END IS THE SUBJECT, NOT A MARKER: the 大掃除 is why the storehouse is being cleared and New Year money is why the shop is busy, which is the audit's fifth divergence answered in the premise rather than in the prose. 店を畳む rather than 廃業 or 閉店 — the audit found 閉店 used for a 銭湯 going out of business, and this is the same error class avoided with a word already in the known set.
stories._premise: CLIMAX: he voids her ticket and the number is the one he spoiled and voided himself in the first week, and that voided ticket is still in his drawer, whole. Both exist. He looks up and she is gone. Nobody explains it, including him. AFTERWORD: see stories-index.md. PREMISE: year-end at a small pawnshop; the owner is clearing the storehouse to close the business by New Year, and one customer comes every month to redeem a comb and pawn it again. WANT: empty the storehouse and close the shop by 大晦日. NEED: to admit the shop was never a business in objects — he keeps perfect records of items and none of people, and that is what lets him take the earlier date. He gets the want; it costs him the thing that would have made having it bearable. SHAPE: three-act, I 1-2, II 3-6, III 7-9. BEATS: 1 counts the stock and voids a torn ticket, number 214 (yes-but, veiled plant). 2 she redeems and re-pawns; he tells her the shop closes (no-and). 3 the record runs back past this book in a third hand (yes-but). 4 next door has been shut on the third for twenty years (no-and). 5 the record says the 15th and her ticket the 16th; he takes the 15th (yes-but, the ugly choice). 6 the dealer pays less than she paid monthly (yes-but, the cost). 7 she comes on the 16th and is not angry; she asks to see the shelf (no-and). 8 her ticket is 214 and the voided one is still in the drawer (yes-but, climax). 9 he closes on schedule; the pale patch stays and he greets an empty doorway (no-and).

new_words.質屋: pawnshop — the setting and the narrator's trade. First occurrence has it doing something rather than being defined: 年末になると、うちのような質屋は忙しくなる. Recurs at the forty-year line and at the closing
new_words.質札: pawn ticket — the object the whole turn runs on. Framed p2 by the act of tearing one and voiding it by number, before the reader has any reason to care. Recurs through every counter scene and at the payoff
new_words.櫛: comb — what is pawned, redeemed and pawned again. Framed p5 by being taken out of a box and set on paper, with its three missing teeth as the only description. Recurs monthly, at the sale, and as the empty shelf
new_words.質流れ: forfeiture of a pawned item once its deadline passes — the mechanism the plot turns on. Framed p15 inside the narrator's own calculation, 十五日で質流れにすれば蔵は予定通り空になる, so it arrives as a consequence he is choosing rather than a term being explained. Recurs at the sale, the confession and the rule
new_words.蔵: storehouse — what the want is about emptying. Framed p1 by the cleaning itself, 蔵を空にするための大掃除. Recurs as where the comb lives, where the old books are, and as the empty room she asks to stand in
